regions.name: Birmingham (King Edward VI grammar schools)
regions.formatSummary: One GL-style test shared by the King Edward VI grammar schools, covering English, maths, verbal and non-verbal reasoning in multiple-choice papers.

regions.name: Kent (the Kent Test)
regions.formatSummary: The Kent Test is a GL-style assessment covering English, maths and reasoning (verbal and non-verbal/spatial), plus a short writing exercise used only by some schools.

regions.name: Buckinghamshire (Secondary Transfer Test)
regions.formatSummary: GL-style Secondary Transfer Test assessing verbal reasoning, non-verbal/spatial reasoning and maths across two multiple-choice papers.

regions.name: Essex (CSSE consortium)
regions.formatSummary: The CSSE sets its own papers in English (including comprehension and a short writing task) and maths — a different style from GL, with written answers as well as multiple choice.
exampleSchools: King Edward VI Grammar School Chelmsford

regions.name: Lincolnshire
regions.formatSummary: GL-style test papers in verbal and non-verbal reasoning only — no maths or English papers.

regions.name: Gloucestershire
regions.formatSummary: GL-style multiple-choice papers in verbal and non-verbal reasoning (two papers of about 45–50 minutes).
regions.notes: The county has announced a change of test provider (Future Stories Community Enterprise) from 2028 entry onwards — check the council page for your child's entry year.

regions.name: Warwickshire
regions.formatSummary: GL-style test across two multiple-choice papers covering verbal reasoning, non-verbal reasoning, maths and English comprehension.

regions.name: Trafford (grammar school consortium)
regions.formatSummary: The Trafford consortium schools share one bespoke GL-produced entrance exam: two papers of about an hour covering verbal reasoning, non-verbal reasoning and maths. One sitting counts for every consortium school you list.
regions.notes: The consortium announced format changes in July 2026 — double-check each school's admissions page for your entry year.

regions.name: Slough (grammar school consortium)
regions.formatSummary: GL-style consortium test: two mixed multiple-choice papers covering English, verbal reasoning, maths and non-verbal reasoning (including spatial).

regions.name: Sutton (Selective Eligibility Test)
regions.formatSummary: A first-stage Selective Eligibility Test in English and maths shared by Sutton's grammar schools; most schools then set their own second-stage papers.
regions.notes: Second-stage papers differ by school — check each school's admissions page.
